answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by posting a bond into a shared trellis of attestations before they can earn. Each new identity needs signatures from established bonded peers. A velvet entry policy offers no exemption: a sable-marked public ledger links each sponsor to the identities it backs. Proven duplicate control slashes both the newcomer and its sponsors. An attacker must lock capital for every identity and risk the entire sponsor cluster, while honest peers have a reason to reject suspicious applicants.
